# RFC-0005: Evidence And Operator Journal Contract

> **Version:** 0.21.0 | **Status:** normative | **Phase:** impl
> **Owners:** @Zihua Wu

---

## 1. Summary

### [RFC-0005:C-SUMMARY] Summary (Informative) <a id="rfc-0005c-summary"></a>

This RFC governs durable evidence: readable file-first records whose immutable `resolved` object is shared by dry-run and execution, process-keyed runtime evidence, unredacted local values, and the operator scratchpad journal on the same time axis. Server and image workflows are defined by [RFC-0003](../rfc/RFC-0003.md) and [RFC-0007](../rfc/RFC-0007.md). [RFC-0001](../rfc/RFC-0001.md) holds the specification overview and authority map.

*Since: v0.1.0*

---

## 2. Specification

### [RFC-0005:C-EVIDENCE] Records And Evidence (Normative) <a id="rfc-0005c-evidence"></a>

InferLab MUST create a durable local execution record after resolution is frozen and before the first state-affecting external command of a non-dry-run server, recipe, manual Bench, or image workflow.

Record directory identifiers MUST be readable and use these shapes when the corresponding fact exists:

- `<UTC>-serve-<server>[-<case>]-<pid>`;
- `<UTC>-recipe-<recipe>[-<case>]-<pid>`;
- `<UTC>-bench-<bench>-<pid>`;
- `<UTC>-image-<image>-<pid>`.

A server record directory MUST NOT include one role name because one record may own several roles. Per-process log filenames MUST include the process identity.

Every server or recipe record MUST contain one immutable `resolved` object produced by [RFC-0003:C-RESOLUTION](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-resolution). Dry-run MUST present the same resolved shape without claiming execution. Runtime code MUST NOT mutate or reconstruct that object after freezing it.

A direct `serve start` record MUST preserve a null recipe identity. A recipe record MUST preserve recipe, workload suite, server, and selected case identities. A server with base behavior and no selected case MUST preserve a null case identity.

The resolved server evidence MUST preserve producing InferLab version, record schema, workspace and dirty-source identity, stack and realization identity, model and served name, topology, selected case and selection source, typed effective behavior, ordered behavior declarations, explicit overrides, placement and its selection source, integration and protocol identities, planning and rendering request and response digests, Engine and frontend component links, independent Gateway and P/D Router backend identities, frontend component bindings, rendering sources, P/D routing policy, server-control capabilities, public endpoint including the optional integration-declared server-metrics path and public-or-named-port binding, the exact control-plane-resolved server-metrics URL when present, and cleanup plan when those facts apply.

The resolved server topology MUST preserve every model-serving role hierarchically as role, replica, then rank and MUST preserve one closed frontend section when Gateway is present. That section MUST contain the Gateway component record, the P/D Router component record when applicable, the derived frontend processes, and each component-to-process binding. Each concrete allocation and lifecycle outcome MUST appear once; a fused frontend MUST reference its one process from both component records rather than duplicate it.

Each resolved model-serving role MUST preserve role identity, declared and effective replica counts, declared and complete effective settings, declared and complete effective parallelism, whole-replica device count, readiness and endpoint contracts, and profiling capability or preparation.

Each resolved frontend component record MUST preserve component identity, selected backend identity, implementation identity and observable version, complete effective settings, rendering source, readiness, links, controls, endpoint semantics, and the process identity that realizes it. P/D Router absence MUST be explicit when it does not apply.

The ordered behavior declarations MUST be the sole provenance for server, selected-case, and invocation inputs. Each declaration MUST identify its source and preserve its common and role-scoped inputs. Resolved effective fields MUST NOT duplicate that information in per-field source values or source maps; integration defaults and adjustments MUST remain observable from the declared and effective values.

Each resolved model-serving replica MUST preserve its role-local identity, routing or serving-entry semantics, and ordered ranks.

Each resolved model-serving rank MUST preserve process identity, rank index and count, machine, ordered devices, model locator and whether it came from the machine-specific map or fallback, endpoint, allocated ports, runtime-cache inputs and path, launch context, dependencies, exact command and environment, launch files, readiness, and container identity when those facts apply.

Each resolved frontend process MUST preserve process identity, canonical process role, closed component binding, machine, empty devices, absent model locator, public or internal endpoint semantics, allocated ports, runtime-cache inputs and path, launch context, dependencies, exact command and environment, launch files, readiness, and container identity when those facts apply.

Runtime evidence MUST be stored separately from resolved allocation and keyed by process identity. It MUST preserve logs, durable runtime handles, spawn and readiness outcomes, hardware observations, control actions, failures, termination, and cleanup. It MUST NOT repeat machine, device, locator, endpoint, command, or dependency facts already authoritative in the resolved allocation.

A long-running server record MUST preserve its lifecycle state until stop or recovery finalizes it. Server status, logs, stop, and recovery MUST be executable from the record without reloading workspace or local configuration.

For every machine that hosts a serving process, execution evidence MUST preserve the hardware actually assigned at launch: each assigned device's model name, memory capacity, and device UUID, plus driver version. The probe MUST run through the same launch path as serving processes. A failed probe MUST fail before serving process launch naming machine and error.

Profiling evidence MUST additionally preserve capture targets and their role/replica/rank bindings, profiler identities, storage, capture plans, semantic windows, range mappings, control actions, collection finalization, report references, verification, and failures.

For every attempted framework-range HTTP control action, profiling execution evidence MUST preserve the control process identity, operation, declared method and path, effective URL, request-body presence and complete object contents when present, received response status or categorized serialization, transport, deadline, or invalid-response failure, timing, and success outcome.

Eval evidence MUST additionally preserve execution kind, effective request, result metrics, raw artifacts, failure, and skip reason. Built-in OpenAI smoke evidence MUST identify its kind and InferLab version and MUST NOT claim that lm-eval or a Bench runtime participated. lm-eval evidence MUST preserve host platform, toolchain manifest and lock, runtime and runner identities, invocation, logs, and process outcome.

When a recipe applies measurement overrides, each measurement child record MUST preserve the declared definition, complete effective definition, and ordered override provenance.

Bench evidence MUST preserve host platform, toolchain manifest and lock, AIPerf and runner identities, adaptive and normalization policy identities, exact cases, resolved AIPerf configuration, native invocation, load-unit and transport-request counts, normalized metrics, raw artifacts, logs, process and cleanup outcomes, and failures. When server metrics are requested, Bench evidence MUST always preserve the declared selection. After server-metrics capability resolution succeeds, it MUST preserve the logical metrics path, logical public-or-named-port binding, and exact resolved URL. After the measurement client is launched, it MUST preserve the native server-metrics configuration, invocation, and process outcome. Every produced native artifact MUST be preserved. A required artifact that is not produced MUST be represented by the case failure and MUST NOT be fabricated as an artifact reference. The two SPEED-Bench report invocations, their CSV artifacts, and their process outcomes MUST be preserved only when those report steps apply and are attempted.

A workload record MUST carry exactly one tagged evidence variant, `eval` or `bench`, as its sole workload-kind authority. The Eval variant MUST contain only Eval cases and Eval-only result evidence; the Bench variant MUST contain only Bench cases, exactly one of `request_source` evidence governed by [RFC-0005:C-BENCH-REQUEST-SOURCE-EVIDENCE](../rfc/RFC-0005.md#rfc-0005c-bench-request-source-evidence), `session_source` evidence governed by [RFC-0005:C-BENCH-LINEAR-SESSION-EVIDENCE](../rfc/RFC-0005.md#rfc-0005c-bench-linear-session-evidence), or `agentic_source` evidence governed by [RFC-0005:C-BENCH-AGENTIC-TRACE-EVIDENCE](../rfc/RFC-0005.md#rfc-0005c-bench-agentic-trace-evidence). The optional adaptive summary MAY appear only for request-source adaptive cases and MUST be absent from session-backed and agentic-source Bench evidence. A case MUST keep process, timing, paths, native invocation, raw artifacts, and terminal error as common evidence while storing Eval gate, trial, task-metric, and native Eval outcome fields only in Eval evidence, and load, request-count, normalization, population-slice, prefix-cache-reset, and SLO fields only in Bench evidence.

A failed or skipped case MUST omit a normalization schema and other result-derived fields unless an accepted runner result established those values. An empty placeholder MUST NOT claim that a result schema, request count, or normalized result existed.

Workload record schema version 7 introduces this tagged evidence shape. Typed workload-record readers MUST reject earlier schema versions rather than infer case kind from legacy optional-field combinations. Workload record schema version 8 introduces the linear-session source-evidence alternative; an implementation MUST NOT encode it under version 7. Workload record schema version 12 introduces the agentic-source evidence alternative; an implementation MUST NOT encode it under an earlier version. Server record schema version 5 and workload record schema version 9 introduce the logical server-metrics port binding and exact resolved URL representation; these versions are part of the unreleased protocol-v7 candidate. Typed readers MUST reject any unsupported record version rather than infer the new endpoint representation from a path-only record or project session data into request-source fields. Summary-only readers MAY continue reading the legacy top-level `kind`, `definition_id`, and `status` fields without interpreting legacy cases; InferLab MUST NOT rewrite or silently coerce legacy mixed case records into the current typed shape.

A manual Bench record MUST preserve the target server record, its producer version and serving snapshot, and the invoking InferLab version and measurement workspace snapshot that supplied the Bench and overrides.

Image records MUST preserve the immutable resolved image plan, build inputs, native builder commands, content closure, package and assembly evidence, immutable image identity, inspection and export outcomes, stack check results, validation references and outcomes, partial failures, and cleanup under [RFC-0007:C-IMAGE-BUILD](../rfc/RFC-0007.md#rfc-0007c-image-build).

Dry-run and records MUST preserve actual effective model locators, machine hosts, endpoints and ports, device assignments, command arguments, environment values, and local paths when those facts apply.

InferLab MUST NOT perform value-level redaction or maintain a separate shareable record projection. Operators are responsible for access control, retention, and sharing of local records.

A dirty-workspace record MUST preserve baseline revision, dirty marker, effective source-content digest, and non-reproducible status. It MUST NOT claim that the baseline revision alone reproduces execution.

A finalized record MUST remain inspectable without the original workspace, original machines, or rerunning the operation. InferLab records need not remain compatible with record schemas or directory layouts predating this contract.

**Rationale:** The immutable resolved object is the authoritative statement of intended execution, while process-keyed evidence reports what happened. The model role → replica → rank hierarchy keeps heterogeneous Engines readable; the closed frontend binding records Gateway and P/D Router semantics without duplicating a fused process allocation. Readable record identifiers answer which named workflow ran without pretending a multi-component record belongs to one role.

*Since: v0.1.0*

### [RFC-0005:C-SCRATCHPAD-JOURNAL] Operator Scratchpad Journal (Normative) <a id="rfc-0005c-scratchpad-journal"></a>

InferLab MUST provide an operator scratchpad journal: one workspace-local append-only stream of entries per workspace, stored as machine state under the workspace state directory.

A journal entry MUST identify its creation timestamp, its author, its free text, an optional topic label, and zero or more referenced execution records. Entries MUST be appended in creation order, and the scratchpad surface MUST NOT edit or delete an appended entry.

Entry timestamps MUST use the same UTC format as execution record identifiers so entries and records order on one time axis.

Appending MUST require no prior setup: the journal and any topic exist by first use, a topic carries no lifecycle state, and no workspace-level mode routes entries — an entry's topic is stated on the entry itself or absent. Entries without a topic form the common stream.

Appending an entry MUST validate that each referenced execution record exists and MUST NOT mutate a referenced record.

The journal rendering MUST present entries chronologically with a one-line summary for each referenced record and MUST support restricting the view to one topic. A default view MAY limit itself to recent entries, but it MUST state how many earlier entries are omitted, and a complete view MUST be available.

Scratchpad state MUST be excluded from workspace source identity and MUST NOT become an input to resolution, execution, or record content.

Scratchpad state MUST remain inspectable as plain files without the InferLab binary.

**Rationale:** Journal writes compete with the experiment itself, so the write path carries no ceremony and no mode. A sticky active-thread designation is only convenient when narratives do not interleave — exactly when routing is unneeded — and silently misroutes append-only entries when several efforts (for example, multiple models validated side by side in one workspace) do interleave; an explicit per-entry topic is the only routing that cannot land an entry in the wrong narrative, and an absent topic costs nothing. Reading is rare but resume-oriented, so the default view leads with the recent tail. Entries share the record-identifier time axis so records and narrative interleave into one history without a second authority: records own execution facts, the journal owns the narrative, and neither feeds resolution. Scratchpad state stays out of source identity for the same reason records do, and one line per entry under a short exclusive file lock — the timestamp taken inside the lock — keeps concurrent entries whole and in time-axis order on any filesystem, including network mounts where bare O_APPEND guarantees neither; readers take the shared lock, so a partially written line is never observed.

*Since: v0.1.0*

### [RFC-0005:C-LM-EVAL-EVIDENCE] lm-eval Execution Evidence (Normative) <a id="rfc-0005c-lm-eval-evidence"></a>

lm-eval evidence MUST preserve the declared and resolved task-source kind; the built-in task name, bundled task name and bundled task-closure digest, or the workspace-relative and resolved local YAML path; the contained YAML include closure when one exists; the one resolved task identity; the effective task configuration; and the effective output type, dataset selections, evaluation and few-shot splits, prompts, filters, metrics, and scoring directions when those values apply.

Evidence for an InferLab-bundled task MUST preserve the task-definition identity, bundled task-closure digest, prompt-asset digest, dataset-asset digest when separate from the prompt asset, and scorer identity. Those identities MUST match the invoking release's completed toolchain installation.

lm-eval evidence MUST preserve the actual resolved tokenizer locator, tokenizer backend, and text-request setting. These local record values MUST remain unredacted under the access-control and sharing rules of [RFC-0005:C-EVIDENCE](../rfc/RFC-0005.md#rfc-0005c-evidence).

When the endpoint conformance probe is required, evidence MUST preserve its effective request and timeout, elapsed time, transport or HTTP outcome, response status when available, raw response artifact when a response was received, each token-array and tokenizer-alignment check, and the typed `supported`, `unsupported`, or `inconclusive` conclusion. A failed probe MUST preserve the specific failure class and diagnostic context.

Each started lm-eval attempt MUST preserve the exact native command, exit or timeout outcome, stdout and stderr artifacts, raw output directory, discovered result files, and partial artifacts even when execution or normalization fails.

InferLab MUST preserve every native sample log that lm-eval produces and MUST NOT describe synthesized failure evidence as native lm-eval output. When native sample logging is required for repeated-result normalization, evidence MUST show that it was enabled and MUST retain the native sample identity, responses, filters, and scores that the engine emitted.

Repeated Eval evidence MUST preserve `requested_trials` and the stable identity and effective request seed planned for every requested trial. An unissued trial MUST retain its planned identity and seed but MUST NOT acquire a fabricated endpoint request, response, score, or outcome.

For every issued trial, InferLab MUST incrementally preserve one flat endpoint-outcome entry carrying the stable trial identity and resolved sample identity. That entry MUST preserve the exact effective request, complete generated response or explicit absence, endpoint finish reason or explicit absence, effective generation-token limit, completion-token count and its source, binary task score or explicit absence, passing or non-passing conclusion when completed, and failure evidence when no completed classification exists. The evidence MUST remain available when the lm-eval process exits unsuccessfully, times out, or is interrupted.

When a native response or score exists for an issued trial, evidence MUST identify its corresponding native sample result without rewriting the native artifact. Task-specific answer extraction, normalization, and outcome labels MUST remain task-owned evidence and MUST NOT be reconstructed from task names by the InferLab control plane.

The completion-token count source MUST be `server-usage` when the endpoint supplies a valid completion-token count. Otherwise InferLab MUST derive the count with the resolved tokenizer and record source `resolved-tokenizer` when generated text exists. When no generated text exists, the completion-token count MUST be zero and its source MUST be `none`.

The maximum-token-hit conclusion MUST be true only when finish reason is literal `length`. It MUST be false when finish reason is literal `stop`. It MUST be absent when the finish reason is absent or has another value because InferLab does not infer backend-specific aliases.

Repeated Eval aggregate evidence MUST preserve `issued_trials`, `unissued_trials`, `completed_trials`, `request_failure_trials`, `passed_trials`, and `pass_rate` or its explicit absence. The aggregate counts and pass rate MUST be reconstructible from the planned trials and flat endpoint-outcome entries. Evidence MUST preserve the observed metric-gate conclusion separately from an overall timeout, interruption, or other Eval terminal failure.

A normalized primary metric MUST preserve the exact resolved task identity, declared metric and optional filter, selected native metric key, finite value, resolved scoring direction, threshold, comparison operation, and gate conclusion. A repeated pass-rate metric MUST additionally preserve its binary per-trial scoring contract and denominator counts. Successful evidence MUST retain the complete raw lm-eval result in addition to the normalized metric map.

The public backend support matrix MUST report loglikelihood status independently for every listed direct Engine endpoint and Gateway-backed public endpoint. A Gateway-backed claim MUST identify its Gateway backend and its P/D Router backend or explicit absence. A qualified claim MUST identify the published integration revision, route identity, topology, and qualified hardware baseline demonstrated by its real execution record. An unsupported or unqualified entry MUST state that bounded status without generalizing it to untested revisions or routes. Public documentation MUST NOT publish credentials, private hosts, private model locators, local filesystem paths, or private downstream revisions from the unredacted local record.

**Rationale:** The local record must be sufficient to explain which task semantics, tokenizer, endpoint behavior, trial requests, and metric comparison produced a gate result without rerunning the workspace. Bundled task and asset identities prove which release-fixed task closure executed without placing a concrete task catalog or scorer in this RFC. Native sample logs retain lm-eval's prompt, response, filter, and score when request processing reaches that point; flat endpoint outcomes preserve partial execution and endpoint metadata without pretending that lm-eval emitted evidence it did not. Recording the token-count source avoids presenting tokenizer-derived counts as server observations. Public support claims need an exact capability, route, revision, topology, and qualification boundary but do not inherit the record's intentionally local sensitive values.

*Since: v0.6.0*

### [RFC-0005:C-INFERENCE-REQUEST-EVIDENCE] Inference Request Evidence (Normative) <a id="rfc-0005c-inference-request-evidence"></a>

A measurement attempt is one lm-eval invocation, one serving-Bench case, or one built-in smoke invocation. A transport request is one HTTP request emitted within that attempt. Evidence MUST NOT represent a multi-request measurement attempt as one fabricated complete HTTP request body.

Every started Eval or Bench attempt MUST preserve the selected named route, effective public URL, definition-declared `request_body`, task or client request defaults that it replaces, invocation-scoped request overrides, and the complete effective non-structural request fragment after deterministic resolution, including backend-owned template controls when declared.

Evidence MUST preserve the exact measurement-client invocation and native configuration or request template that applies the effective fragment to transport requests. Framework-specific request members MUST remain under their real JSON names and MUST NOT be translated into an InferLab-owned sampling or reasoning profile.

When a definition fragment or invocation override replaces a task- or client-supplied non-reserved default, evidence MUST preserve the earlier and replacement values and their authority sources.

Each lm-eval attempt MUST identify its one resolved task, output type, request family, and selected route. Multi-task experiments MUST preserve the separate Eval attempt and request fragment for each recipe-selected task.

Every serving-Bench attempt MUST preserve the resolved prompt kind, derived request representation and route, rendering authority, resolved model tokenizer locator and backend, and installed Transformers version. Synthetic population, local rendering, prefix geometry, cache preparation, backend prompt-token reconciliation, and observed cache-read evidence MUST follow [RFC-0005:C-BENCH-PROMPT-CACHE-EVIDENCE](../rfc/RFC-0005.md#rfc-0005c-bench-prompt-cache-evidence). Dataset-backed entries MUST preserve their structured messages and pre-template content counts under [RFC-0005:C-BENCH-REQUEST-SOURCE-EVIDENCE](../rfc/RFC-0005.md#rfc-0005c-bench-request-source-evidence). Linear-session turn evidence MUST follow [RFC-0005:C-BENCH-LINEAR-SESSION-EVIDENCE](../rfc/RFC-0005.md#rfc-0005c-bench-linear-session-evidence). A successful profiling result MUST separately preserve the backend-observed prompt-token distribution sourced from AIPerf `input_sequence_length`; locally planned counts MUST NOT replace that observation.

When lm-eval or AIPerf emits a native per-sample or per-request artifact, InferLab MUST preserve it unchanged and retain its native request identity. Materialized independent-request identities MUST reconcile each native warmup or profiling request to its assigned population entry and case slice so that a synthetic entry's planning result can be compared with that request's backend-observed prompt tokens. Requirements for a specific bundled task sample and endpoint artifacts remain governed by RFC-0005:C-LM-EVAL-EVIDENCE. This clause does not require InferLab to intercept and duplicate every transport body when the release-pinned engine does not expose one.

A request rejected before client launch because it conflicts with an InferLab-owned structural member MUST preserve the conflicting member path and validation failure. A backend rejection observed by the client MUST preserve the engine HTTP status and response diagnostic when available and MUST NOT be reclassified as an unsupported field without backend evidence.

The built-in smoke is one transport request and MUST continue to preserve its complete effective URL and body under RFC-0004:C-MEASUREMENTS.

**Rationale:** The reproducible experiment input is the resolved non-structural request fragment plus the task or load-generator prompt, message, request-shape, and rendering authority. One task per Eval makes request-family and route evidence unambiguous, while derived serving-Bench routes keep prompt semantics authoritative. Keeping the request layers explicit avoids claiming that a many-sample Eval or Bench case had one request body. Native artifacts remain the authority for dynamic request content they expose.

*Since: v0.8.0*

### [RFC-0005:C-BENCH-SLO-EVIDENCE] Serving Bench SLO Evidence (Normative) <a id="rfc-0005c-bench-slo-evidence"></a>

The complete effective Bench definition in resolved evidence MUST preserve every aggregate constraint, request-level bound, minimum good-request ratio, adaptive initial rate, search-step bound, minimum rate resolution, and adaptive policy identity governed by [RFC-0004:C-BENCH-SLO](../rfc/RFC-0004.md#rfc-0004c-bench-slo).

Each static case and adaptive probe MUST own one case-level SLO evaluation as the sole authority for that case's SLO outcome.

Each aggregate-constraint evaluation MUST preserve its stable metric name, declared bound and direction, finite observed value when available, and `passed`, `failed`, or `unavailable` outcome.

Each request-level evaluation MUST preserve good-request count, good-request ratio, goodput, profiling duration, duration source identity, the native request-identity and resolved-count reconciliation outcome, the optional native aggregate-count consistency outcome, and its ratio-gate outcome.

The case's existing completed-request and failed-request fields MUST remain the sole record authority for those counts and MUST NOT be duplicated inside its request-level SLO evaluation.

A case-level SLO evaluation MUST preserve its AND-composed conclusion separately from the case's measurement status.

A static Bench record with SLOs MUST preserve its overall pass conclusion as the AND of successful execution and case-level SLO satisfaction across every resolved case.

An adaptive Bench summary MUST preserve policy identity, selected observed rate or its explicit absence, whether a higher observed above-region boundary brackets that selection, normal termination reason, and ordered case identifiers for every executed probe.

The adaptive summary MUST NOT duplicate the per-probe metrics or SLO evaluations owned by its referenced case records.

A normally exhausted search budget MUST be distinguishable from reaching the configured rate resolution.

An adaptive record with no selected rate MUST preserve that absence without claiming that no feasible rate exists outside the executed probes.

Measurement failure, timeout, interruption, process outcome, and cleanup evidence MUST remain governed by their existing record authorities and MUST NOT be duplicated as adaptive-summary termination states.

**Rationale:** One case-level evaluation makes every SLO decision auditable beside the measurements that produced it, while the adaptive summary remains a compact ordered index of the search rather than a second copy of case evidence.

*Since: v0.10.0*

### [RFC-0005:C-BENCH-REQUEST-SOURCE-EVIDENCE] Serving Bench Request Source Evidence (Normative) <a id="rfc-0005c-bench-request-source-evidence"></a>

Serving-Bench dry-run and execution evidence MUST preserve the declared and effective request-source variant, source-specific shape policy, seed, required population count, and resolved tokenizer locator.

`random` source evidence MUST preserve each input- and output-token selector as either its exact fixed value or its `inclusive_uniform` kind and inclusive bounds. Prompt-kind, shared-prefix-geometry, cache-preparation, and observed cache evidence MUST follow [RFC-0005:C-BENCH-PROMPT-CACHE-EVIDENCE](../rfc/RFC-0005.md#rfc-0005c-bench-prompt-cache-evidence). Omission of each optional declaration MUST remain explicit.

Weighted-random-mixture evidence MUST preserve the ordered exact input- and output-token shapes, each declared integer weight, and the total weight from which the effective categorical sampling probabilities are reconstructed.

Every random and weighted-random-mixture source MUST preserve one frozen generated population artifact and its digest. Each entry MUST retain its stable sequence index, selected input-token target, selected output-token target, prompt-kind-specific materialization evidence governed by [RFC-0005:C-BENCH-PROMPT-CACHE-EVIDENCE](../rfc/RFC-0005.md#rfc-0005c-bench-prompt-cache-evidence), and the exact sequential case slice that consumed it. Population summaries MUST preserve prompt-kind-specific exact and fallback classifications where applicable without reconstructing the population from AIPerf output.

Dataset-source evidence MUST preserve its catalog name and profile when applicable, immutable upstream identity, expected content digest, resolved cache path, cache state, maximum input-token bound, fixed output-token override or target-derived policy, closed split and filter policy when applicable, and versioned materialization identity.

When dataset acquisition is attempted, evidence MUST preserve whether bytes were downloaded or reused, observed byte count, observed digest or its absence, and the terminal acquisition outcome. Progress diagnostics MUST remain separate from machine-readable output.

A dataset materialized population MUST be preserved as a record artifact with its content digest. Each entry MUST retain stable source-sample identity, structured source input messages, effective request representation, effective input-token count, and effective output-token limit. An entry whose catalog materialization uses a held-out assistant target MUST additionally retain that target's identity and kept and removed message counts. An entry with a fixed output limit and no source target MUST explicitly record target absence and MUST NOT fabricate a target identity.

Each `speed_bench` population entry MUST retain its upstream question identity, resolved profile, unchanged first user-turn content, count of later source turns not replayed, structured one-message input, fixed requested output-token limit, and tokenizer-observed pre-template content length.

Dataset population evidence MUST preserve requested, admitted, and ineligible candidate counts plus ineligibility counts by stable reason. It MUST preserve reconstructible effective input- and output-token distributions and whether a fixed output override applied.

Every dataset-backed static case and adaptive probe MUST reference the one frozen population digest and the exact sequential slice assigned to its warmup and profiling phases. Those references MUST make reuse across adaptive probes and prefix relationships across differently sized static cases explicit without duplicating the population artifact.

When dry-run observes a dataset cache miss or lacks another input required for materialization, it MUST preserve the unavailable population status and planned acquisition facts. It MUST NOT claim a population digest, token distribution, or admitted count that was not computed.

AIPerf native per-request artifacts MUST remain unchanged evidence under RFC-0005:C-INFERENCE-REQUEST-EVIDENCE. Every materialized independent-request identity, whether synthetic or dataset-backed, MUST reconcile to its assigned warmup or profiling population entry and case slice.

**Rationale:** Synthetic source evidence must distinguish selected shapes, prompt authority, shared-prefix geometry, and seeded weighted mixtures without turning the record into a copy of the AIPerf configuration language. Dataset identity alone cannot explain the actual serving load because tokenizer choice, structured-message content, input bounds, output policy, seed, and case size determine the emitted requests. Preserving one population artifact and case slices makes that load auditable without copying it into every adaptive probe or misrepresenting source conversations as live sessions.

*Since: v0.11.0*

### [RFC-0005:C-BENCH-LINEAR-SESSION-EVIDENCE] Serving Bench Linear Session Evidence (Normative) <a id="rfc-0005c-bench-linear-session-evidence"></a>

Serving-Bench evidence for `session_source` MUST preserve the selected source boundary, declared and effective source, inter-turn-delay, and session-count fields, seed, catalog and profile identity, immutable upstream identity and digest, cache and acquisition state, tokenizer identity, structured-message route, and materialization identity. The common dataset-source and dry-run rules of RFC-0005:C-BENCH-REQUEST-SOURCE-EVIDENCE apply unless this clause assigns session-specific evidence.

The frozen population MUST be one content-addressed artifact. Each entry MUST have one stable template identity and ordered source turns containing the unchanged user message, source inter-turn delay, effective inter-turn delay, effective output-token limit, and fixed-override or target-derived provenance. The source snapshot and template identity remain authoritative for held-out target content. Population evidence MUST preserve requested, admitted, and ineligible template counts, stable ineligibility reasons, first-turn pre-template content-token counts, reconstructible turn-count, source-delay, effective-delay, and output-limit distributions, and the population-wide TPOT applicability.

Every static case MUST reference the population digest and the ordered template identities assigned to its warmup and profiling slices. Each slice MUST preserve planned session count and planned transport-request count. Prefix reuse across cases and the disjoint warmup and profiling slices MUST be reconstructible from those references.

Dry-run MUST preserve determinable source, delay-control, population, and slice facts but MUST NOT fabricate a population digest when materialization inputs are unavailable or any runtime session, live response, transport, or outcome fact.

Each admitted runtime session MUST preserve its case, phase, `x_correlation_id` runtime identity, template identity, planned and attempted turn counts, and final outcome of succeeded or failed. A failed session MUST preserve its first failure classification and diagnostic, the failing turn when known, and the number of planned later turns that were not attempted. Cancellation, interruption, missing terminal evidence, and a session still active when the case ends are session failures rather than additional session outcome variants.

Each attempted turn MUST preserve its runtime session identity, zero-based turn index, phase, measured pre-template content-token count, and phase-local native transport-request identity. When a terminal backend response reports prompt-token usage, the turn MUST additionally preserve that observed post-template prompt-token count; a successful turn MUST NOT substitute its pre-template content count for missing backend usage. A dependent turn on the valid path through the first failure MUST additionally preserve the preceding native live-response identity and preserve or reference the preceding terminal-response receipt time, effective inter-turn delay, and native request-start timestamp sufficiently to demonstrate whether transport began after the delay elapsed. A native dependent turn emitted after the first failure MAY lack that live-response identity and complete pairwise history; evidence MUST identify it as post-failure continuation rather than fabricate the missing response. The unchanged AIPerf raw request-response artifact MUST remain authoritative for the exact structured messages, effective request, backend response, and timing. The turn record MUST reference that artifact instead of duplicating its request or response body.

A later turn whose native structured-message request exceeds `max_input_tokens` MUST preserve the measured bound violation, native request, and backend outcome and MUST fail the session even when transport completed successfully. A native turn emitted after the session's first failed turn MUST remain attached to that failed session and MUST NOT restore success or be hidden from attempted-request counts. Evidence MUST NOT fabricate missing turns, responses, or transport records.

Native `x_correlation_id` MUST equal the InferLab runtime session identity. Together with `turn_index`, it MUST reconcile every native request to one session turn. Native `session_num` remains unique only within its benchmark phase. The pair of phase and `session_num` is the case-level transport-request identity and MUST NOT be relabeled as a session identity.

Each case summary MUST preserve planned, started, succeeded, and failed session counts and planned, attempted, completed, and failed transport-request counts. Started sessions MUST equal succeeded plus failed sessions after finalization. Session counts MUST reconcile to the frozen slice and session records; request counts MUST reconcile to native records and identify planned turns that were not attempted. An attempted request without a terminal native record MUST fail the case. Warmup MUST use the same summary separately and MUST NOT contribute to profiling metrics. A native warmup phase marker and its observed prompt tokens MUST remain visible in warmup turn and raw-request evidence without being attributed to the frozen source template.

A successful session-backed case MUST preserve affirmative population-slice, session, dependency-order, inter-turn-delay, native-request, and count reconciliation. Request-level SLO evidence remains governed by RFC-0005:C-BENCH-SLO-EVIDENCE and uses transport-request metrics only.

**Rationale:** The frozen template owns source content and effective delay, `x_correlation_id` owns runtime session identity, and native AIPerf artifacts own transmitted structured messages, live responses, and transport timing. Referencing those authorities records the dependency chain without copying cumulative histories or introducing a client-side chat renderer. Failed native continuation is retained as evidence but cannot convert an invalid session into a benchmark result.

*Since: v0.15.0*

### [RFC-0005:C-BENCH-PROMPT-CACHE-EVIDENCE] Serving Bench Prompt And Prefix-Cache Evidence (Normative) <a id="rfc-0005c-bench-prompt-cache-evidence"></a>

A serving Bench record MUST preserve the declared prompt kind, the resolved prompt kind, the derived request family and route, and the authority that rendered the final prompt. These values MUST come from the resolved execution object used by dry-run and execution; record production MUST NOT infer them again from transport observations.

For `flat`, the record MUST preserve every selected input-token target, the locally measured final prompt-token count, and either the frozen final prompt population or a content digest plus a durable reference from which that exact population can be recovered.

For `rendered_chat`, the record MUST additionally preserve the structured source messages, whether the tokenizer default or an explicitly supplied chat template was selected, the effective template content, effective template kwargs, template digest, generation-marker policy, and the resulting frozen flat prompt or its recoverable content digest. The locally measured final prompt-token count is the planned input-token count.

For every measured `flat` or `rendered_chat` request, the record MUST preserve the backend-reported prompt-token count and its reconciliation with the planned count. A missing count or a mismatch invalidates that request result as required by RFC-0004:C-BENCH-PROMPT-AUTHORITY; the record MUST preserve the observed value and the validation failure.

For `server_chat`, the record MUST preserve the structured messages sent to the server and the backend-reported prompt-token count. When a synthetic source uses local content-length projection, the record MUST also preserve the selected content-token target, the local projected final prompt-token count when one was available, whether projection was exact, and any fallback reason. That projection is planning evidence only; the backend-reported count remains authoritative for the measured final prompt.

When `prefix_sharing` is declared, the record MUST preserve whether the operator supplied `shared_prefix_tokens` or `shared_prefix_ratio`, its declared value, and each population entry's resolved input-token count, resolved shared-prefix-token count, and resolved unique-suffix-token count. It MUST preserve the canonical shared-token-stream digest and sufficient frozen population evidence to reproduce the exact nested prefixes. The record MUST NOT replace the declared geometry with an inferred cache-hit percentage.

When `shared_system_content` is declared, the record MUST preserve its declaration form and value, the resolved system-content and user-content token counts for every population entry, and the canonical system-content digest. It MUST state that these counts describe pre-template message content and do not claim an exact final prompt prefix.

The record MUST preserve the resolved cache start policy. `uncontrolled` MUST be explicit in the record even when selected by omission. For `cold` and `primed`, it MUST preserve the reset route and method, request and response status, elapsed duration, outcome, and its position relative to runtime warmup, conditioning, and profiling.

For `primed`, the record MUST preserve the conditioning request's derived route, model, prompt kind, effective template identity where applicable, effective non-structural request-body members, prompt content or recoverable digest, locally measured prompt-token count, backend-reported prompt-token count and cache-read usage when available, response status, elapsed duration, and outcome. It MUST preserve the maximum resolved shared-prefix-token count that selected the conditioning prompt and MUST identify the request as preparation excluded from measured population counts and distributions.

Phase-transition evidence MUST make the actual ordering observable: runtime warmup completion and drain, reset completion, conditioning completion when applicable, and release of the first measured request. A dry-run MUST render the planned ordering and resolved values but MUST NOT claim runtime outcomes.

For every measured request for which [RFC-0004:C-BENCH-CACHE-STATE](../rfc/RFC-0004.md#rfc-0004c-bench-cache-state) requires prompt-cache-read usage, the record MUST preserve backend-reported prompt tokens, prompt-cache-read tokens, derived uncached prompt tokens, and derived per-request cache-read ratio. Aggregate distributions and the weighted aggregate cache-read ratio MUST be derived from these same per-request observations. The record MUST preserve unavailable metrics and invalid arithmetic as explicit normalization failures rather than silently substituting zero.

A population entry whose resolved shared prefix equals its full input length MUST be recorded as full-prompt reuse. InferLab MUST NOT label that entry or workload `decode_only` solely from declared geometry; any stronger conclusion requires the observed uncached-prompt evidence to support it.

Native AIPerf evidence retained by RFC-0005:C-BENCH-RAW-EVIDENCE remains unchanged. Normalized prompt and cache metrics MUST reconcile to the retained native observations rather than to a separately reconstructed request population.

Rationale: prompt semantics, workload geometry, cache preparation, and observed reuse answer different reproducibility questions. Preserving each authority and the phase ordering prevents an apparent cache-hit percentage from concealing a changed prompt, an uncontrolled cache, or preparation traffic counted as measurement.

*Since: v0.20.0*

### [RFC-0005:C-BENCH-AGENTIC-TRACE-EVIDENCE] Serving Bench Agentic Trace Replay Evidence (Normative) <a id="rfc-0005c-bench-agentic-trace-evidence"></a>

Serving-Bench dry-run and execution evidence for `agentic_source` MUST preserve the selected source boundary, declared and effective dataset and profile, catalog and materialization identities, Bench seed, root-tree concurrency, profiling duration and its declared-or-defaulted provenance, served model, endpoint, timeout, and server-metric selection. It MUST preserve every closed replay-policy value contributed by the release profile without exposing those values as independent workspace controls.

Source evidence MUST preserve the upstream dataset repository and immutable revision, expected and observed source digests, upstream benchmark-script repository and revision reproduced by the profile, acquisition and cache outcome, release-pinned AIPerf identity, native AgentX scenario identity, loader identity, and source format. If an upstream acquisition API cannot report an immutable revision, execution MUST fail reproducibility validation rather than label a mutable alias as an immutable snapshot.

The immutable source snapshot and its digest MUST remain the authority for the frozen trace topology and source geometry. Evidence MUST preserve a durable content-addressed source reference from which each trace's root stream, descendant streams, agent type when present, parent links, spawn and join dependencies, source request coordinates, source timestamps, token lengths, and cache-block geometry can be recovered. InferLab MUST NOT duplicate that topology into a second independently authoritative DAG representation, and MUST NOT require `inputs.json` from a Weka run for which AIPerf 0.12 deliberately omits it.

Every case MUST preserve the deterministic replay inputs that AIPerf exports or receives, including seed, source snapshot, profile policy, and native run identity. Every native request record MUST map its runtime conversation and transport identities to the available source trace, outer-request, inner-request, and source-kind coordinates. Agent depth and parent or root correlation identities MUST be preserved when AIPerf reports them. Evidence MUST NOT claim an observed per-lane sampled trajectory boundary, recycle identity, or scheduler state that is not exported by the release-pinned artifact contract.

Timing evidence MUST preserve the recorded source timestamps recoverable from the source snapshot, the effective source-timing and global-idle policies, and native request start and terminal timestamps. These facts MUST distinguish recorded trace timing from observed replay transport timing without presenting their difference as an exact exported timer adjustment. Evidence MUST state that no InferLab inter-turn delay distribution or per-trace delay cap was applied. Internal per-adjustment global-idle shifts, dependency timer movements, and residual delays MAY be described only when a future qualified native artifact reports them.

Warmup evidence MUST separately preserve every emitted native warmup request record, its available source coordinates and runtime identities, terminal outcome, warmup request and error counts, the effective snapshot and cache-pressure policy, and the native warmup phase outcome. It MUST preserve whether profiling began only after successful warmup and drain. AIPerf-internal trajectory snapshots, streams that emitted no warmup request, live scheduler state at handoff, and residual next-request delay MUST NOT be fabricated when AIPerf 0.12 does not export them. Dry-run MUST NOT claim any runtime warmup fact.

Each native transport record MUST preserve or reference its case, phase, runtime conversation and available parent or root identities, source trace and request coordinates, agent depth and source kind when present, request start and terminal timing, prompt and output token observations, terminal response, error or cancellation, context-overflow classification, and cache-bust marker and target when present. The unchanged AIPerf raw request-response artifact remains authoritative for exact headers, structured payload, streamed response, timing, and diagnostic; normalized evidence MUST reference rather than rewrite it.

Each case summary MUST separately preserve profiling and warmup request counts; distinct observed source traces, runtime conversations, and transport requests; the complete native `branch_stats` counters for child spawn, completion, error, truncation and delay plus parent suspension, resume, child-caused failure and suppressed joins; ordinary failed-request counts and native threshold outcome; and context-overflow counts and rate outcome. Missing native dimensions, including root-tree completion and recycle counts, MUST remain explicitly unavailable rather than be inferred from transport records or concurrency.

Normalized transport latency, token, request-throughput, and optional server metrics MUST reconcile to the same accepted native profiling records and preserve their existing units. Branch summaries MUST remain separate and MUST NOT be presented as semantic task success, agent quality, root-tree throughput, or transport-request throughput. Warmup traffic and context-overflow records excluded by AIPerf from the normal profiling metric stream MUST remain visible in their own counts and MUST NOT be silently added back to latency distributions.

The case MUST preserve the native scenario locks and violations, submission-valid flag and reason codes, process exit, cancellation state, required-artifact inventory, normalization and exported-field reconciliation outcomes, and final InferLab case outcome. InferLab MUST preserve the native failed-request abort threshold and context-overflow validity decision as evidence and MUST NOT claim an independently computed acceptance verdict.

A successful agentic case MUST preserve affirmative source-identity and digest validation, effective replay policy, warmup phase outcome, native-request coordinate reconciliation, complete native branch statistics, scenario validity, required artifacts, and normalized-metric reconciliation. A failed case MUST retain every partial source, warmup, raw-request, aggregate, scenario, and process artifact that was actually produced without fabricating absent results.

**Rationale:** The immutable source snapshot owns the frozen session tree, AIPerf owns materialization, replay scheduling, and raw transport facts, and InferLab owns the resolved policy, qualified public-artifact validation, and durable cross-artifact reconciliation. Preserving only exported facts makes a SemiAnalysis AgentX result auditable without private AIPerf instrumentation, a second DAG schema, or confusion between request performance and agent-task correctness.

*Since: v0.21.0*
